summary: Channel focus is GLP-1, so all candidates are GLP-1 topics. The plague topics carried over from earlier snapshots are left out on purpose: they're outside the current focus. The best openings right now are fresh, checked research that creators haven't picked up yet. 1) GLP-1 and nail detachment (EADV 2026: 39% of users vs 9% of non-users). ScienceDaily covered it today and we found almost no creator video coverage. 2) The pilot RCT on weight regain after stopping a GLP-1: about 10.75% regain with usual care vs about 3.6% with an app or medically tailored meals. 3) The retatrutide TRIUMPH-2 decoder (20.8% weight loss in people with type 2 diabetes; Lilly plans to file in Q1 2027). Search interest is high because of 'What is RETA?' questions, but it needs a strict warning about gray-market sellers. Other emerging items with solid sources: no link found between semaglutide and pancreatic cancer in the Nordic registries (HR 0.91), the Lancet trial on semaglutide and heavy drinking, the STEP UP liver-fat sub-analysis, and the tirzepatide + ixekizumab psoriasis trial. For news hooks on access and safety, cover Novo's list-price cuts from Jan 2027 and the NPR report on GLP-1 lawsuits, both framed calmly. Microdosing is rejected under brand rules. Playbook fit: named-drug and named-study titles with one plain number have been our strongest. Keep 'talk to your doctor or prescriber' in every piece. Never promote compounded, gray-market or telehealth price-shopping sources.

candidates.topic: GLP-1 medicines and nail problems: first controlled study finds nail detachment reported by 39% of users vs 9% of non-users (EADV 2026)
candidates.angle: 'Ozempic nails' explained calmly. What the study found (575 users vs 1,329 non-users, self-reported, cross-sectional, not yet peer reviewed). Why it shows a link, not cause. Possible explanations researchers raise, such as rapid weight loss and nutrition, framed as hypotheses. Practical: eat enough protein and see your prescriber or a dermatologist if your nails change. Pair with the earlier hair-loss findings.
candidates.why_now: Presented at EADV (Sep 30–Oct 3). It moved from medical outlets (HCPLive, Medical Economics, Advisory Board) to ScienceDaily and Gizmodo today, Oct 12. It's a classic pattern of going from press release to science news to creators, and our searches found almost no creator videos yet.

evidence.signal: Nail detachment 39% vs 9%; discoloration 46% vs 17%; 575 users vs 1,329 controls
GLP-1 users report more nail detachment and hair loss than nonusers
Mainstream healthcare-industry pickup
Consumer tech/science pickup ('hair loss was just the start')

candidates.topic: Stopping a GLP-1: pilot RCT finds structured support (wellness app or medically tailored meals) cut 4-month regain from about 10.75% to about 3.6%
candidates.angle: Plan for the off-ramp, positively. Regain after stopping is well documented (e.g. STEP 1 extension). This small pilot (n=39) hints that structured support may slow it. Habits that support you on or off the medicine: protein, strength training, meal structure. Make clear that any decision to stop belongs with your prescriber. No stopping advice.
keywords: what happens when you stop glp-1
how to keep weight off after wegovy
candidates.why_now: Published in Obesity Science & Practice Oct 7, with coverage from News-Medical (Oct 12), Newsweek, MedicineNet and Epocrates. 'What happens when you stop' is one of the most-searched GLP-1 questions, and this gives it a new hook.

evidence.signal: Pilot RCT, Preventing Weight Regain After GLP-1 Discontinuation
Control +10.75% vs app +3.60% vs meals +3.58% over 4 months; n=39
Mainstream pickup
Trial registration

candidates.topic: Retatrutide TRIUMPH-2: up to 20.8% weight loss at 80 weeks in adults with type 2 diabetes. What 'RETA' is and why it isn't approved yet
candidates.angle: Named-drug decoder with a question title, e.g. 'Retatrutide: What Did TRIUMPH-2 Actually Find?' Explain the triple agonist (GIP, GLP-1, glucagon) and the results by dose without giving dosing advice: 12.7%, 19.1% and 20.8%, with A1C down up to 1.6%. Lilly plans to file with FDA in Q1 2027. Explain plainly that it's investigational and not available by prescription. Lilly is suing gray-market 'research' sellers, and those products are not medicine.
candidates.why_now: Lilly's TRIUMPH-2 topline came Sep 30. TCTMD, Drug Topics and Women's Health covered it (Oct 9–11), WCNC ran a 'VERIFY: What is RETA?' piece (Oct 12), and Lilly's lawsuits against copycats are in WaPo and STAT. Named-drug trial decoders are our best long-form format (EloraTZP 216 views).

evidence.signal: TRIUMPH-2: 20.8% at 80 weeks on 12 mg; BLA planned Q1 2027
Lilly suits over copycat versions

candidates.topic: Does semaglutide raise pancreatic cancer risk? Nordic registry study of 97,464 users found no link (HR 0.91)
candidates.angle: A myth correction that reassures with evidence. A regulator-mandated study across Denmark, Sweden and Norway: 131 cases among semaglutide users vs 123 in the comparison group, and no dose or duration effect. Be honest about the limits: it's observational, funded by Novo and limited to type 2 diabetes. Say 'no link found', not 'ruled out'.
candidates.why_now: Presented at EASD (Sep 28–Oct 2), and headlines picked it up again on Oct 12 (Bioengineer). Cancer fear is a constant search driver, and lawsuit coverage (NPR) keeps safety questions in view.

evidence.signal: 97,464 semaglutide users; HR 0.91 (95% CI 0.71–1.16); no dose/duration effect
Study design: active-comparator new-user cohort, 2018–2023

candidates.topic: Semaglutide and heavy drinking: Lancet RCT in people with alcohol use disorder and obesity found heavy-drinking days fell 13.7 percentage points more than with placebo
candidates.angle: A benefit beyond weight, kept to its evidence. The trial had 108 adults over 26 weeks; cravings and liver markers also improved. It isn't approved for alcohol use disorder. Explain the brain-reward mechanism in plain words. Anyone struggling with alcohol should talk to a clinician.
candidates.why_now: Medical Economics flagged it Oct 11, and EMJ and PsyPost have also covered it. Mad In America's skeptical take on marketing GLP-1s for addiction (Oct 10) shows debate is building, which leaves room for a balanced explainer.

evidence.signal: RCT: heavy drinking days −13.7 pp vs placebo; n=108; published in The Lancet
Consumer science pickup

candidates.topic: Ozempic and Wegovy US list prices drop up to 50% from Jan 1, 2027 (about $675/month), plus the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge $50 copay. What it means for you
candidates.angle: A calm decoder of access news. Explain list price vs what you actually pay: insurance, Medicare and the manufacturers' official self-pay programs. Bring questions to your prescriber or insurer. Never point people to compounded or no-prescription providers (e.g. the '$99/month' headlines).
candidates.why_now: Medical Economics (Oct 11) and Stocktwits/BofA are discussing the cuts, ABC7 is covering the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge, and the Boston Globe ran an op-ed on insurer limits. Cost is the top question our audience has.

evidence.signal: List prices cut up to 50% from Jan 1, 2027; ~$675/month; self-pay unaffected
Price cut also applies to Wegovy pill and Rybelsus

candidates.topic: GLP-1 lawsuits and serious side effects: what's alleged (gastroparesis, bowel obstruction, sudden vision loss) and why NPR says we don't know how often
candidates.angle: Honest and steady. Lawsuits are allegations, not measured rates: about 4,400 plaintiffs vs about 31 million US adults using GLP-1s (KFF). Name the warning signs that mean you should call your doctor (severe or persistent vomiting, severe abdominal pain, sudden vision changes) and explain why reporting side effects matters. No fear-bait, and no advice to stop the medicine.
candidates.why_now: NPR's piece ran on many public-radio sites Oct 7–10. Vision-loss lawsuit stories (Sep 22), AFRO's 'hidden risk' piece and the J Intern Med review on serious adverse events (Oct 9) all add to it.

evidence.signal: Serious side effects alleged; unclear how often
Review: GLP-1 RAs and serious adverse events: evidence, uncertainty
Thousands of plaintiffs in consolidated litigation

candidates.topic: Semaglutide and fatty liver: STEP UP sub-analysis found 23 of 26 adults with excess liver fat reached normal levels (<5%) by week 72
candidates.angle: Benefits beyond the scale: liver fat. Mean liver fat fell from 8.8% to 3.1% in a 55-person MRI sub-analysis. Be clear about the limits: post hoc, small, no placebo comparison shown. Link it to the broader MASH evidence and to habits that help the liver.
candidates.why_now: EASD data, with Pharmacy Times (Oct 10) and Patient Worthy coverage. Fatty liver is a high-search, underserved metabolic topic.

evidence.signal: Semaglutide normalized liver fat in most adults with obesity

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide plus ixekizumab for psoriasis with obesity: TOGETHER-PsO found 40.6% reached completely clear skin vs 29.0% with ixekizumab alone
candidates.angle: Psoriasis and weight are connected. Explain the 'immunometabolic' link simply, and that treating obesity alongside a psoriasis biologic did better in this Lilly-funded phase 3b trial. Questions to ask a dermatologist. Not an ad: refer to the medicines generically.
candidates.why_now: New biomarker data came Oct 9 (Fall Clinical Derm), with coverage from HCPLive, Dermatology Times, pharmaphorum, Clinical Trials Arena and NewsNation. Psoriasis communities are a niche our competitors don't serve.

evidence.signal: PASI 100 40.6% vs 29.0% at 36 weeks; durable at week 52
Phase 3b superiority on PASI 100 + ≥10% weight loss

candidates.topic: Feeling awful on a GLP-1? Under-eating, dehydration or a passing bug may be part of it, plus how to make common side effects easier
candidates.angle: A friendly 'getting the most from GLP-1' explainer. Low energy can come from eating too little and drinking too little. Practical, evidence-based tips: protein-first small meals, fluids, eating slowly, and stopping when full. When to call your prescriber. No dose-adjustment advice.
keywords: why do i feel sick on wegovy
candidates.why_now: Yahoo Creators ran 'Feeling awful on your GLP-1?' on Oct 11. As cold and flu season starts, more people will be asking whether it's the medicine or a bug.

evidence.signal: Illness vs side effects; under-eating and dehydration as causes
Clinician field notes on mild but common GLP-1 effects

candidates.topic: Wegovy pill vs Wegovy shot: how oral semaglutide compares, and early US uptake (JAMA Netw Open)
candidates.angle: A plain comparison naming both sides: how each is taken (daily pill vs weekly shot, in general terms), what the trials show, and questions to bring to a doctor. No switching advice.
keywords: how effective is the wegovy pill
candidates.why_now: A JAMA Netw Open study on early uptake (Oct 1), Physician's Weekly coverage (Oct 9) and a Yahoo doctor explainer (Oct 10). People are searching 'how effective is the wegovy pill'.

evidence.signal: Early adoption and diffusion of oral semaglutide in US adults with obesity

candidates.topic: GLP-1 medicines and sleep apnea: new meta-analysis of RCTs, plus tirzepatide's SURMOUNT-OSA results
candidates.angle: A benefit beyond weight for a very common condition. Across RCT meta-analyses, the AHI (pauses in breathing per hour) fell. In SURMOUNT-OSA, tirzepatide cut AHI by about 20–24 events/hour vs placebo. Treatment is used alongside CPAP rather than replacing it; discuss with a sleep doctor.
candidates.why_now: A new Sleep and Breathing meta-analysis (Oct 6) refreshes an evergreen pillar. Sleep searches pick up around the daylight-saving change (Nov 1 US).

evidence.signal: GLP-1 RAs for OSA: meta-analysis of RCTs
Where GLP-1 drugs fit in sleep apnea care

candidates.topic: Orforglipron, the oral non-peptide GLP-1 pill: what the trials show for weight, diabetes and blood pressure (ATTAIN-HYPERTENSION design)
candidates.angle: 'The GLP-1 pill you don't take on an empty stomach': explain how a small-molecule GLP-1 differs from injectable peptides, summarize results from the Cureus systematic review, and note the trial now testing it for high blood pressure. Re-check its exact FDA status at publish time.
candidates.why_now: A Cureus systematic review (Oct 11), Medical Dialogues coverage (Oct 12) and the ATTAIN-HYPERTENSION design paper. A Nature Medicine phase 3 trial of a rival oral small molecule (safiglipron) adds 'pill race' context. Our earlier orforglipron long-form was at the median (14), so use a question-decoder title.

evidence.signal: ATTAIN-HYPERTENSION phase 3 design
Oral small-molecule safiglipron phase 3 vs dapagliflozin

candidates.topic: GLP-1 and heart failure: tiny CardioMEMS study shows lower lung-artery pressure as weight fell
candidates.angle: Use only as one beat in a 'heart benefits' piece next to SELECT and the HFpEF trials (STEP-HFpEF, SUMMIT). This study had only 9 patients, so present it as an early signal, never as a headline.
candidates.why_now: HCPLive covered it Oct 11. Weak on its own, but it gives a fresh hook to the evergreen 'heart benefits' pillar.

evidence.signal: n=9; mean PA pressure 27.3→24.3 mmHg over 6 months

candidates.angle: Rejected under brand rules (no microdosing or self-titration content), even framed as 'why to avoid'. If needed, fold one generic line into side-effects pieces: 'dose decisions belong with your prescriber.'
candidates.why_now: Firstpost (Oct 12) and recurring social trend, but off-limits for InforMed.

evidence.signal: Why you should avoid microdosing weight-loss drugs
